ideas.title: SmartSub: local captions with highlighted keywords
ideas.hook: Free offline captions burned into your TikToks, with topic words highlighted
ideas.why: Pain point: TikTok views stuck at ~250 (Oct 21-28) and the one post with a topic-first caption did best (346). The Lab's 'Keyword-first captions' upgrade is approved but needs a way to make on-screen captions fast. Beat AutoClip (made to cut long videos, needs LLM key and Python 3.11 setup), OpenMontage (huge, paid APIs) and oh-my-cassette (montage editing, 4 months old).
ideas.format: TikTok · Runs on: Laptop (Windows, CPU is fine) · 20 min setup
ideas.script: Replaces: typing or CapCut-style captions by hand (or none). What it adds: drop in your talking video, local Whisper writes the subtitles offline, you fix the odd word, then it burns them in with ffmpeg and can highlight chosen terms in a colour. Setup: download the signed Windows installer from Releases, install, set acceleration to CPU-only, choose a small English model (base/small), run one test video. It also has a CLI/MCP so Claude Code can run it later. I read the code in a sandbox: no analytics or obfuscated code found, runs without API keys. I did not run the desktop app itself (it is a GUI). Risks: README has a sponsor ad and many Chinese-platform features you can ignore; 63 open issues; CPU transcription of a 60 s clip may take a minute or two. Check in a week: do captioned videos get more views than the ~250 baseline, and does captioning cost under 5 minutes per video?
ideas.buildPrompt: I'm Omar, a student in Mississauga with a TikTok self-improvement page. I film short sit-down talking videos and my views are stuck around 250, so I want every video to have burned-in captions with the key topic words highlighted. Please set up SmartSub (https://github.com/buxuku/SmartSub, MIT licence, official repo, Windows installer on its Releases page) for me. Steps: 1) Walk me through downloading the signed Windows x64 installer from the Releases page and installing it on my Windows laptop (I have no strong GPU, so set Engines & Models to CPU-only and pick a small English Whisper model such as base or small). 2) Show me how to drop in one of my talking videos, transcribe it locally, fix any wrong words, and burn the subtitles in with big bold text at the lower-middle of a 9:16 video. 3) Read docs/docs/guides/automation-reference.md in the repo and show how to use the highlightTerms and highlightColor options (or the styling UI) so the 1-3 topic keywords in each caption line (for example 'liking gap', 'Stoicism') stand out in a bright colour. 4) Write me a short checklist I can follow for each video, and tell me how long it takes per 60-second video on CPU. Do not create accounts, do not enter any API keys, and keep everything local. Do not use the translation, dubbing or sponsor features. If you use Claude Code, only use SmartSub's own CLI/MCP from a throwaway folder and never give it my passwords or tokens.

items.title: SmartSub: local subtitles with burned-in keyword highlights
items.creator: buxuku/SmartSub
items.whyItWorks: KEPT. Windows installer, CPU fallback, local Whisper, burn-in captions with highlightTerms, Claude Code MCP/CLI. Fits the approved keyword-first captions upgrade.

items.title: AutoClip: long video to captioned 9:16 clips
items.creator: artbyjazi/autoclip
items.whyItWorks: REJECTED. Built to cut clips out of long videos; Omar films short sit-down videos. Needs Python 3.11, ffmpeg-full and an LLM key or Ollama; pre-1.0.

items.title: OpenMontage: agentic video production system
items.creator: calesthio/OpenMontage
items.whyItWorks: REJECTED. Huge (100+ tools, 423 open issues), many pipelines lean on paid APIs; his render.py pipeline already works.

items.title: oh-my-cassette: AI montage editor for Claude Code
items.creator: Cassette-Editor/oh-my-cassette
items.whyItWorks: REJECTED. Montage editing; he already has a visual-hooks skill and his videos are talking heads or sims. Created June 2026, too new to trust.

items.title: youtube-mcp-server: YouTube API for AI assistants
items.creator: ZubeidHendricks/youtube-mcp-server
items.whyItWorks: REJECTED. Agent HQ collectors already pull his channel stats hourly; needs OAuth setup for no new insight.

items.title: Remotion: videos with React
items.creator: remotion-dev/remotion
items.whyItWorks: REJECTED. Custom licence (not plain OSS; paid for some commercial use) and a JS stack when his pipeline is Python.

items.title: Kokoro-FastAPI: local TTS server
items.creator: remsky/Kokoro-FastAPI
items.whyItWorks: REJECTED. Good, but he has no voiceover pain right now (ambience channel, talking-head TikTok).

brief.headline: Free offline captions with highlighted keywords for TikTok
brief.summary: No requests from you this week. My best find is SmartSub: a free Windows app that transcribes your talking videos on your own laptop and burns in captions, with the option to highlight keywords. It fits the keyword-first captions upgrade you approved, since your views are stuck near 250. I looked at 7 repos and rejected the rest as too big, too paid or not matching your pipeline.
filmToday: SmartSub — install it and caption one talking video as a test
notes: Only one pick: nothing else beat what you already use.
SmartSub's README has a sponsor ad and lots of Chinese-platform features; ignore them. I read the code but did not run the desktop app.
